prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger for Scotland: The SNP’s 2015 manifesto pledges to shake up an out‑of‑touch Westminster so it serves Scotland better. A vote for the SNP is a vote to make Scotland’s voice heard more loudly, deliver progressive politics, and never put the Tories into power. If there is an anti‑Tory majority, the SNP will work with others to lock the Conservatives out and press Labour to deliver real change.

Ending austerity, investing in people and services
- Replace deep cuts with modest, responsible spending increases; reduce debt as a share of income.
- Progressive taxation: those on the highest incomes contribute more; crack down on avoidance; restore 50p top rate; bank levy/bonus tax; mansion tax; abolish non‑dom status.
- Protect and strengthen the NHS: increase UK health spending by £9.5bn above inflation by 2020‑21, delivering £2bn more for Scotland; oppose privatisation.
- Raise the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the Living Wage; curb exploitative zero‑hours contracts.
- Expand free childcare to 30 hours a week for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds.
- Fair welfare: scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt and reform Universal Credit and PIP; reverse DLA replacement; increase Carer’s Allowance to match JSA; fairer sanctions; increase work allowance by 20%.
- Protect pensioners: retain triple lock; back a £160 single‑tier pension; review raising the state pension age; keep winter fuel allowance.
- Cut household energy bills; tackle fuel poverty; ensure pre‑payment users get fair prices.

Jobs, growth and regional rebalancing
- Invest in infrastructure (transport, housing, broadband, energy) to boost productivity and create well‑paid jobs.
- 100,000 affordable homes a year UK‑wide; extra capital for Scottish housebuilding.
- Connect Scotland to HS2 with north–south build; accelerate superfast broadband/4G and introduce a Universal Service Obligation.
- Seed‑fund the Scottish Business Development Bank; expand export finance; protect small firms with prompt‑payment laws; increase Employment Allowance to £6,000.
- Cut Air Passenger Duty by 50% then abolish; consider VAT cut for hospitality; restore post‑study work visas.
- Support oil & gas jobs, deploy the Oil & Gas Authority in Aberdeen, and internationalise the supply chain.
- Create a Sovereign Wealth/Energy Fund from natural resource revenues; City Deals for all Scottish cities; fair share of CAP convergence for farmers; protect Royal Mail USO.

Energy, climate and communities
- Back offshore and onshore wind, hydro, CCS, and community energy; reform transmission charges; deliver islands interconnector; grow the Green Investment Bank.
- Continue fracking moratorium; match Scotland’s carbon targets; establish a Climate Justice Fund.
- Keep 1,000 extra police; retain Scottish court fines; restore VAT exemptions for Police Scotland and Fire.

Democracy, rights and equality
- EU: oppose withdrawal; require a UK‑wide “double majority” for any exit; secure devolved roles in EU decisions; exempt NHS/Scottish Water from TTIP.
- Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; oppose blanket surveillance (“snoopers’ charter”).
- Political reform: STV for elections; scrap the House of Lords; meaningful MP recall; votes at 16.
- Equality: 50% women on public boards; equal pay audits; end VAT on sanitary products; improve race and maternity protections; reform immigration detention.
- Media: devolve broadcasting; give BBC Scotland a fairer licence‑fee share (+£100m) to boost the creative sector.

Defence and foreign affairs
- No new nuclear weapons; stop Trident renewal and redirect funds to public services.
- Strengthen conventional defence footprint in Scotland; transparency in MoD spending; better support for veterans.
- Ethical internationalism: maintain 0.7% aid; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy; support a two‑state solution for Israel/Palestine.

Home Rule
- Deliver Smith in full, then go further to full fiscal responsibility; devolve welfare, employment policy (including the minimum wage), business taxes, National Insurance and equality—so Scotland can build a fairer, more prosperous nation.
